title: mass-gap-horizonless: a horizonless branch in the lower black-hole mass gap and its gravitational-wave signatures
description:
Reproduction package for the paper A horizonless branch in the mass gap and its gravitational-wave signatures. Contains the curvature-tower mechanism and its cap, the mini-theorem on the impossibility of a degenerate inner horizon in the tower, the horizonlessness criterion and the threshold mass range, echoes and time delays, the tidal deformability, the validated f-mode computation, the baryon budget, and the quasinormal-mode results. Every number is reproduced by one command from a clean clone; the map from each number to its script and result file is in docs/reproducibility.md.

A tower of curvature terms caps curvature without invoking exotic matter and produces a branch of horizonless ultracompact objects that can populate the lower black-hole mass gap. The branch is constrained, not detected: its echo amplitudes are already partly excluded by O3, and its f-mode spectrum does not violate the universal f–Λ–M relation, so asteroseismology cannot discriminate it. The discriminators are the mass range and the tidal deformability.

Scope, stated here and not only in the repository: the central observational statement is a range, not a single mass. The branch criterion carries a shape factor running over [0.18, 0.39], which spreads the upper mass of the horizonless branch by a factor 2.2; quoting a single threshold mass would misrepresent the calculation. The echo amplitudes originally reported were a windowing artefact and have been corrected. The branch does not explain the emptiness of the 3.5–5 solar-mass region and makes no prediction about how populated it is.

The f-mode solver is RelModPy by Fabian Gittins, vendored unmodified under its own MIT licence in src/third_party/relmodpy/ and not covered by this repository's licence. This work's contribution around it is the equation-of-state adapters and the replacement of the library's root finder. Otherwise: code in src/ and figures/ is MIT; data in data/, raw logs in logs/ and the generated figure images are CC-BY-4.0.

The calculations were carried out with automated agents under the author's direction, with an independent cross-audit between two separate research projects. The author is responsible for the results.
